project.name: Profile-Guided Resource Orchestration Platform for Multi-Step Agentic Workflows

scope_items.S1: Workflow Orchestration System (DAG-based, topological execution over multi-step agentic workflows)
scope_items.S2: Profile-Guided Allocation (heuristic scoring, model+hardware+config assignment, drift-correction)
scope_items.S3: Testing and Evaluation (fault injection, cost/latency/reliability comparison vs fixed allocation)

concepts.name: Profile-Guided Optimization (real measured data drives allocation)
MILP joint solver for task/model/hardware assignment
Curve-level routing metrics (nAUC, Peak Score, QNC, RCI)
Standardized-tooling design pattern for fair comparison harness
Model-combination-level selection (assign models per pipeline role jointly, not per call)
Multi-armed bandit / arm-elimination search over a combinatorial config space
Client-side (developer-controlled) optimization vs server-side serving optimization
Framework-agnostic transport-layer interception/attribution for measuring per-call cost/latency

papers.full_citation: Chaudhry, G. I., et al. (2026). Murakkab: Resource-Efficient Agentic Workflow Orchestration in Cloud Platforms. OSDI '26.
papers.summary: Declarative workflow compiled to a DAG; a Profile-Guided Optimizer (MILP) jointly assigns model, hardware, and parallelism per task, solved once per workflow instance, using real profiled cost/latency/reliability data rather than assumptions.

full_detail.problem: [RECONSTRUCTED FROM PRIOR-SESSION SUMMARY, NOT RE-DERIVED FROM THE ORIGINAL PDF] Existing agentic workflow systems fix model/hardware assignment at design time or make per-call decisions without a holistic, whole-DAG view, leading to inefficient resource use in cloud deployment of multi-step agentic workflows.
full_detail.method: Declarative workflow specification compiled into a DAG. A Profile-Guided Optimizer inspects the full DAG before execution and solves a MILP that jointly assigns model + hardware/resource + parallelism configuration per task, using profiled (measured, not assumed) cost/latency/reliability data. Decision is made once per workflow instance, not per call.
full_detail.results: [Not re-derivable without the source PDF — original session's extracted numbers are not preserved in the handoff summary.]
full_detail.limitations: MILP requires a specialized/licensed solver (CPLEX/Gurobi/GLPK-class), does not adapt to drift without a full re-solve, and is heavyweight relative to the compute/engineering budget of a one-semester student project.

concept_links.detail: Murakkab is the origin of the whole-DAG-before-assignment framing this project adopts.
Origin of the Profile-Guided Optimization concept: real measured data, not assumptions, drives allocation.
Murakkab's optimizer core is a MILP; this project explicitly replaces it with a heuristic while keeping MILP as an optional offline baseline.

papers.full_citation: Cheng, J., & Nguyen, D. T. (2026). Scalable Joint Resource Allocation for SLO-Constrained LLM Inference in Heterogeneous GPU Clouds. arXiv:2604.07472.
papers.role_label: Strongest technical precedent found so far for the MILP-to-heuristic move
papers.summary: [RECONSTRUCTED FROM PRIOR-SESSION SUMMARY] Introduces a Greedy Heuristic / Adaptive Greedy Heuristic for SLO-constrained LLM inference resource allocation across heterogeneous GPU clouds, reporting 260x+ speedup over exact solving with near-optimal cost and graceful degradation under uncertainty. Introduces C_FEASFIRST (feasibility-first filtering before cost-ranking).

full_detail.method: Greedy Heuristic / Adaptive Greedy Heuristic that performs feasibility-first filtering (discard infeasible allocations under SLO constraints) before cost-based ranking of remaining candidates.
full_detail.results: 260x+ speedup relative to exact (presumably MILP-class) solving, near-optimal cost, graceful degradation under uncertainty.
numbers: 260x+ speedup vs exact solving (as reported in prior-session summary)

concept_links.detail: Direct LLM-specific precedent for replacing an exact/MILP-class solver with a fast heuristic, the core move this project makes.
Origin of the feasibility-first-then-cost-rank pattern, reusable in this project's own DAG-walking allocator.

papers.full_citation: Ong, I., Almahairi, A., Wu, V., Chiang, W-L., Wu, T., Gonzalez, J. E., Kadous, M. W., & Stoica, I. (2024/2025, ICLR). RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data. arXiv:2406.18665.
papers.role_label: Evaluation-metric source; scope mismatch on core mechanism
papers.summary: [RECONSTRUCTED FROM PRIOR-SESSION SUMMARY] Routes individual queries to one of two existing LLMs using human preference data. Flagged as a scope mismatch: this is model *selection between existing LLMs* per query, not joint model+hardware+config allocation across a DAG. Useful for its PGR/APGR-style quality-cost evaluation metrics.

full_detail.method: Learns a router, trained on human preference data, that assigns each incoming query to one of two candidate LLMs (a strong/expensive model or a weak/cheap model).
full_detail.limitations: Per-call, two-model routing — does not address joint multi-resource (model+hardware+parallelism) allocation across a multi-step workflow, which is this project's actual problem.

concept_links.detail: Represents the learned per-query routing paradigm this project's problem differs from (whole-DAG, multi-resource allocation vs per-call two-model routing).
Source of PGR/APGR-style quality-cost evaluation metrics usable in this project's own evaluation methodology.

papers.role_label: Evaluation methodology source; same scope mismatch as P4
papers.summary: [RECONSTRUCTED FROM PRIOR-SESSION SUMMARY] Same per-query routing scope mismatch as RouteLLM. Useful for online preference-based evaluation methodology and curve-level metrics (nAUC, Peak Score, QNC, Routing Collapse Index), plus a standardized-tooling design pattern for building a fair comparison harness — feeds this project's Scope Item 3 (Evaluation), the best-covered scope item in the map.

full_detail.method: Online, preference-based evaluation methodology for LLM routers, using curve-level metrics rather than single-point accuracy: nAUC, Peak Score, QNC (Quality-Normalized Cost, or similarly named), and Routing Collapse Index (RCI). Provides standardized tooling for building a fair comparison harness across routing methods.
full_detail.limitations: Same scope mismatch as P4 — evaluates per-query routing among existing models, not multi-resource DAG-level allocation.

concept_links.detail: Source of the online preference-based evaluation methodology this project's own evaluation plan can borrow from.
